ctx: John 8 is one long argument in the temple courts. The closing verses fix the scene:

ctx.q: He spoke these words in the treasury, teaching in the temple

ctx: . John tells his Gospel in the language of a courtroom. The words testify and testimony run through chapters 5 and 8, and Jesus' opponents keep demanding proof.
This study follows Deuteronomy 19. There the rule is read in a courtroom. Here it is quoted back by the man on trial.

inv.q: You testify about Yourself; Your testimony is not true

inv: , the Pharisees say. They are not inventing a rule. They are applying Deuteronomy 19:15: one voice cannot establish itself. If Jesus had waved the rule away, he would have conceded that he stood outside the law. He does the opposite.
He answers in two moves. First he defends the quality of his testimony:

inv.q: Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is true, because I know from where I came and where I am going

inv: . A witness is only as good as his knowledge, and he claims knowledge his judges lack. Then he meets the rule head on:

inv.q: And even in your Law it has been written that the testimony of two men is true

inv: . Your law, he says, and he does not correct it. He treats the law of witness as binding on himself.

inv.q: I am the One testifying about Myself, and the Father having sent Me testifies about Me

inv: . Two voices, the Son and the Father, satisfy the rule as Moses wrote it. A claim that looked like a man vouching for himself is a claim with two witnesses behind it, one of whom the room cannot see. Their next question shows they grasped the point:
Carry one puzzle forward. In John 5:31 Jesus says the opposite:

inv.q: If I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is not true

inv: . The two sentences do not contradict. In chapter 5 he grants the rule's terms and goes on to call witnesses; study 5 follows him through it. In chapter 8 he shows why his testimony stands once the rule is met. Both times he argues under Deuteronomy 19.

w: The rule both sides accept. Study 1.
x.q: by the mouth of two witnesses, or by the mouth of three witnesses, shall every word be established

w: The same concession in the same Gospel. Study 5 follows it.
x.q: If I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is not true

w: The Father named again as the second witness.
x.q: the Father Himself, has testified concerning Me

w: The apostle John reasons the same way: if we accept human testimony, God's is greater.
x.q: the testimony of God is greater

take: Jesus does not escape the law of witness. He fulfils it by naming his second witness. If he submitted to the rule, no one else stands outside it.
